Case Study: Classifying a Drone's Equations

Read the passage carefully, then answer the 5 MCQs in the test below.

In an aerospace control laboratory, engineers describe how a drone responds to commands using differential equations, and their first job is always to classify each equation before choosing a method of solution. Classification records two numbers. The order is the order of the highest derivative that appears; the degree is the power of that highest derivative once the equation has been written as a polynomial in its derivatives, with every radical cleared. When a derivative sits inside a function such as sine, no polynomial form exists and the degree is simply left undefined. The team also notes that the number of independent arbitrary constants in a general solution equals the order, which tells them how many initial sensor readings must be supplied. Today they tabulate four sample equations from the flight-control manual and record each order and degree carefully.

questions.explanation: The highest derivative present is (d²y)/(dx²), so the order is 2. (b).
The highest derivative is second order, so order =2; it is raised to the power 2, so degree =2. The cube on the lower-order term does not affect the degree. (c).
Here sin (dy/dx) cannot be turned into a polynomial in the derivatives, so no polynomial form exists and the degree is not defined. (d).
Squaring gives 1+(dy/dx)²=((d²y)/(dx²))²; the highest derivative is order 2 raised to power 2, hence order 2, degree 2. (a).
